I use iPhone Mirroring every day to access my iPhone right from my Mac, and it's about to get even better this year. The public betas of iOS 27 and macOS 27 Golden Gate are out this month, bringing three major updates to iPhone Mirroring. Here's everything new.

macOS 27: New iPhone Mirroring Features

The biggest change to iPhone Mirroring in macOS 27 is the ability to resize the iPhone Mirroring window.

As my colleague Marcus reported last week, you can now resize the iPhone Mirroring window for any app that's compatible with iOS 27. For now, this only works with Apple's native iPhone apps. However, once developers start rolling out iOS 27 updates later this year, support for window resizing will expand quickly.

Previously, iPhone Mirroring on macOS only offered three preset sizes: Smaller, Actual Size, and Larger. Changes in macOS 27 Golden Gate and iOS 27

expected to launch later this year.

There are a few more iPhone Mirroring updates in macOS 27 and iOS 27:

  • Control Center Access
  • DRM Video Support

Previously, iPhone Mirroring gave you no access to Control Center at all. In macOS 27, you can access it using the CMD+4 keyboard shortcut, or via the View menu in the Mac menu bar.

DRM video support means you can now watch copyright-protected video content through iPhone Mirroring on your Mac. Previously, when iPhone Mirroring was enabled, any DRM-protected video would just display a black screen.

macOS 27 also gives iPhone Mirroring a new app icon, which is different from many other built-in Apple apps.

How often do you use iPhone Mirroring on your Mac? Are you excited about these changes in iOS 27 and macOS 27? Have you tried them in the public beta? Let us know in the comments.
